text:
anya: Quick check — Primus-11B onboarding status. I pushed weights to s3://redwood-models/primus/11b/v1/ and uploaded tokenizer `primus-tokenizer-v1.zip`. Running a quick smoke bench and seeing a tokenizer quirk: 'co-op' splits into ['co', '-', 'op'] which breaks a couple of our tests. Also, what's the expected default max_seq_length here: 2048 or 4096?

matt: For similar 11B families we use 4096. Tokenizer split looks like byte-level or a pretokenizer rule. Can you paste the tokenizer.json?

anya: Pasting minimal tokenizer.json snippet:```json
{"do_lower_case": false, "special_tokens": ["</s>", "<pad>"], "normalizer": "nfc", "pretokenizer": {"type": "byte_level"}, "added_tokens": []}
```

jia: That's the hint — byte_level will split on punctuation. We had this with Pegasus variants. Two options: switch to a WordPiece-like pretokenizer or add a rule to treat '-' as part of a token. You can try adding `treat_as_whitespace": ["-"]` or swap pretokenizer to `metaspace` depending on training.

sam: For perf notes: on 80GB A100s we saw best p50 latency at batch 8 and seq=2048. For seq=4096 batch 4/8 is usually the sweet spot — memory is the limiter. I'm happy to run the perf sweep once you confirm seq. Use `perf-bench` with `--warmup 20 --runs 200`.

devops-bot: perf-runner: queued job #4321 for model primus-11b on node-pool catalog-small (requested 2 gpus, 80GB A100)

anya: Confirming: set max_seq_length=4096, initial batch=8, kv_cache_shards=2 (to avoid memory spike). Kicking off:```bash
perf-bench --model s3://redwood-models/primus/11b/v1/ --tokenizer primus-tokenizer-v1.zip --seq 4096 --batch 8 --warmup 20 --runs 200 --out s3://bench-logs/primus11b/2405556666/
```

matt: small thing — manifest shows a different sha256 for weights v1 compared to what was uploaded earlier. @anya can you re-verify the checksum before the run finishes? If mismatch, we should re-upload with `upload-tool --stage model` to avoid serving stale files.

anya: Good catch. Noted a transient network error during upload. Re-uploading now, will post checksum.

ci-bot: upload-tool: upload complete for primus/11b/v1, manifest updated, checksum 3a7f9d2b4c5e6f7890abc123def4567890abcdef1234567890abcd1234ef5678, job id 9876

jia: If latency looks high, try the int8 quant path — we have a recipe `internal/qrecipes/primus11b-q8.yaml` that keeps quality within 0.5 BLEU/EM on our eval set and reduces memory enough to raise batch size. Also consider enabling prefix KV caching for common prefixes.

anya: Perf run started. Early live strip (after warmup): p50=95ms, p90=210ms, throughput~32 tok/s (measured on a short seq=1024 probe). Full logs uploaded: s3://bench-logs/primus11b/2405556666/full.log

sam: :thumbsup: those p90s look fine as a starting point. If p90 > 350ms on full 4096 runs we should toggle prefixing and re-run. Also add `--measure p50,p90,p99,throughput` to the job (if not already).

matt: I'll keep a rollback plan ready in the rollout doc (internal/rollouts/primus11b). If we see tokenization regressions in production tests, we should pin to the old tokenizer and re-evaluate.

anya: Thanks all — I'll wait for full results and post a short summary. If anyone wants the raw checkpoint or tokenizer to validate locally, ping me and I'll share a signed link.

sam: ping me once the full p99 numbers are in, I'll correlate with infra traces.

(end of thread)
